To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monoclonal antibody (mAb) 1E5B5 recognizes a novel antigen (NS-1) expressed by murine natural suppressors (NS) cells.
a novel NS-1 antigen expressed by a subset of murine NS cells can be detected by a rat mAb, and that this antigen is not present in other cell types.
monoclonal antibody (mAb) 1E5B5 reacts with a unique 50 kDa antigen expressed on a murin NS cell subset, and that mAb 15E5.B5 can be used to isolate and enrich for NS cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel phenotypically unique murine cell subset which we believe may be the long sought-after NS cell.
the development and characterization of a novel NS cell-specific mAb.

the identification, characterization, and purification of murine NS cell populations and their antigenic markers, and the development of monoclonal antibodies which are specific for these cells and their unique phenotypic markers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mAb 2E5.B5 recognizes a novel 50kDa NS cell-associated protein, NS-1, which is expressed on a subpopulation of murine NS cells, and is not expressed on other murine null cell types.
mAb 5E1.B5 is a useful reagent for the study of NS cells.
mAb 5E5.B5 is a unique and useful reagent for the identification and purification of NS cells, and that the 50 kDa protein NS-1 is a unique phenotypic marker of NS cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mAb 2E5.B5 is a useful reagent for identifying a novel NS cell-associated antigen and for isolating NS cells from a heterogeneous cell population.
NS-1 is a novel phenotypically distinct cell surface antigen which is expressed by some, although not all, NS cells.
mAb 5E5.B5 recognizes a unique NS-1 antigenic marker which is expressed by some, and perhaps all, SPANS cells and by a subset of CY-spleen and NB spleen NS cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 1E5 antigen is not a general marker for NS cells, but rather is a unique antigen expressed on a specific subset of NS cells.
the mAb 1 E5.B5 recognizes a unique phenotypic marker that is expressed by a subpopulation of murine natural suppressors, and is absent from other null cells.

NS-1 is expressed on a subset of murine NS cells, but not all NS cells, and that this unique phenotypic marker may provide a means for the identification of NS cell subsets and the study of NS cell biology.
